gaps.sentence: If the temperature ___ below freezing tonight, the race will be postponed.
gaps.explanation: First conditional: present simple in the if-clause, will + infinitive in the result.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ me, I would have helped you move house.
gaps.hint: a missed request in the past
gaps.explanation: An unreal past condition takes the past perfect: had asked.

gaps.sentence: They would have won the match if their best player ___ injured.
gaps.hint: unreal past needs the past perfect
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition requires the past perfect: had not been.

gaps.sentence: What will you do if the train ___ before you get there?
gaps.explanation: Even in questions about the future, the if-clause uses the present simple: leaves.

gaps.sentence: I wish we ___ longer, but our train leaves at six.
gaps.explanation: 'Wish' plus 'could' expresses regret about present ability: could stay.

gaps.sentence: If they ___ that the bridge was unsafe, they would have closed it years ago.
gaps.explanation: A past unreal condition takes the past perfect: had known.

gaps.sentence: He wishes he ___ harder at school when he had the chance.
gaps.hint: past regret, wish plus past perfect
gaps.explanation: Regret about past behavior takes the past perfect after 'wish': had worked.

gaps.sentence: If she ___ the lottery, she would travel the world.
gaps.explanation: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + infinitive.
